newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says coalition deal still fair way off.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says coalition deal still fair way off.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters told reporters on Thursday after a three hour and 50 minute meeting with the ruling conservative National Party that a coalition deal was "still a fair way off".
Asked if he was close to an agreement with National, Peters said: "The fact is we have a lot of work to do with both sides today and for all of the rest of the week."
Peters said NZ First, which holds the balance of power after the October 12 election, would not be drawn into a debate with the left-wing Alliance Party about its needs and wants.
He said he had always understood the left-of-centre Labour Party would be talking to the Alliance if and when it was appropriate, as was happening at present.
Peters said he had written to the Alliance last week setting out NZ First's position, and the Allianc'es response had been cordial and positive.
"I don't intend to be part of any debate or any ping pong match from one party to another," Peters said.
NZ First is in its sixth week of talks with both Labour and National about forming a coalition government.
